issues.title: ci(guard): make class:guard and class:docs actually check something

labels.name: class:guard
labels.description: Adds or repairs a check, gate or CI condition. Self-merge on green with a recorded RED run.

issues.body:
## What this is

Ruling R1 (`RULED_2026-08-10_pr-self-merge-and-four-more.md`) lets a seat merge
the **guard** and **docs** classes without Pip, on green. The labels `class:guard`
and `class:docs` were created in three repos on 2026-08-10 and, until this PR,
they **promised eligibility and nothing checked anything** -- the same defect that
retired `ship:hotpatch-48h` on the same day. This PR is the mechanism.

New workflow `.github/workflows/self-merge-eligibility.yml` (pull_request:
opened, labeled, unlabeled, synchronize, edited), backed by
`tools/check_self_merge_eligibility.py` and 29 hermetic tests in
`tests/test_check_self_merge_eligibility.py`.

| situation | verdict |
|---|---|
| no class label | PASS, neutral -- never blocks a normal PR |
| `class:docs` | PASS only if EVERY changed path is documentation |
| `class:guard` | PASS only if the PR body records the RED run (Section 5g) |
| `needs:pip` + a class label | FAIL -- a label cannot lift a hold |
| both class labels | FAIL -- a PR is one class or neither |

Design, failure-message style and the "declaration plus a mandatory substantive
reason" rule are adopted from `tools/check_ladder_bump.py`, not reinvented.

**Documentation, for the docs class, means:** a path under `docs/`, or a file
ending `.md` / `.rst` / `.txt` -- **excluding** machine-read `.txt` files
(`ladder_version.txt` is the leaderboard board key, `version.txt` is the version
SSOT, `requirements*.txt` are pins, `godot/build_stamp.txt` and
`godot/steam_appid.txt` are shipped engine data) and vendored `godot/addons/`.
A suffix-only rule would have waved the board key through as prose.

**One judgement call, flagged for overruling.** `needs:pip` **alone**, with no
class label, is neutral rather than red: a hold nobody is trying to skip is not
this gate's business, and a check that reddens every held PR is a check everyone
learns to ignore. It fails the moment a class label tries to lift the hold. One
constant, `BLOCKED_FAILS_ALONE`, flips it.

## Section 5g: the RED run

This PR was opened carrying `class:guard` with **no declaration in the body**, on
purpose, so the new gate would fail on this very PR for the exact rule it exists
to enforce.

RED-RUN: https://github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/actions/runs/31487755114 -- opened with class:guard and no declaration in the body; the gate failed itself before it was believed

That run is red at `Check this PR against its class label`, printing the expected
format. The self-test step above it was green in the same run: the rule table
(11 red/green cases) and the 29 unit tests ran before the gate judged this PR.
This line is what turns it green -- so the check's own green is downstream of its
own red.

DO NOT MERGE -- reporting back first.

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issues.title: input(dev): ESC/pause disables ALL diagnostic surfaces -- root cause is process_mode, not input priority

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
Raised by Pip while playtesting 2026-07-30, verbatim:

> "esc menu seems to override dev menu, maybe those should have different overall weight? dev should probably override everything so can diagnose / bug report / issues etc with menus?"

The design ask is right. The mechanism is NOT the one the symptom suggests, so this
was investigated before proposing a fix.

## What is actually happening (CONFIRMED from source)

The operative mechanism is `process_mode`, not input handling order.

1. `godot/scripts/ui/pause_menu.gd:87` -- `show_pause_menu()` does
   `get_tree().paused = true`.
2. `godot/scenes/pause_menu.tscn:19` -- `process_mode = 3`
   (`PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`). The pause menu is the only surface in the frame
   deliberately exempted from the pause it just caused.
3. `godot/autoload/keybind_manager.gd:280` `_input()` is where BOTH diagnostic
   surfaces are actually dispatched from:
   - `:301-303` `debug_overlay` (F3) -> `debug_overlay_toggled.emit()`
   - `:306-308` `dev_mode` (backslash) -> `dev_mode_toggled.emit()`
   Neither `godot/scripts/debug/dev_mode_overlay.gd` nor
   `godot/scripts/debug/debug_overlay.gd` defines an `_input()` of its own --
   grep confirms zero `_input` / `_unhandled_input` in either file. The dev
   overlay subscribes to the signal at `dev_mode_overlay.gd:56`.
4. `KeybindManager` is an autoload (`godot/project.godot` `[autoload]`) with **no
   `process_mode` override**. Grep over `godot/autoload/*.gd` finds exactly two
   files that set one -- `leaderboard_sync.gd:49` and `update_check.gd:67`, both
   `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`. KeybindManager inherits, i.e. pausable.

INFERRED (not verified by running the game, which is out of scope while main is
frozen): therefore, the instant the pause menu opens, `KeybindManager._input()`
stops being called at all, and **every global hotkey dies -- backslash, F3, F6
flight recorder, F7 UI-evolution shot, screenshot, log export**. The
`get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` at `pause_menu.gd:94` is a red herring:
it fires only inside the `KEY_ESCAPE and visible` branch, so it consumes ESC and
nothing else.

The converse direction Pip actually observed has the same root:
`godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:498-505` opens the pause menu on ESC with no test
for whether the dev overlay is open (it cannot test -- the overlay has no input
claim). So ESC with the dev overlay up pauses the tree underneath it. The
overlay stays *visible* (a CanvasLayer keeps drawing) but its dev-poke Buttons go
dead, because `main_ui.gd:326-328` adds it as a child of MainUI, which is
pausable. `DebugOverlay` (`godot/scenes/main.tscn:416`) is likewise a child of
the pausable main scene root. That is exactly "esc menu overrides dev menu".

Secondary, INFERRED, and *not* the operative cause here: Godot dispatches
`_input` in reverse tree order, so the main scene's nodes are polled before
autoloads added earlier at the root. A scene-level `set_input_as_handled()` can
therefore pre-empt KeybindManager in the unpaused case. Worth knowing, but no
current binding collides.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than shrugging at

Pip's stated reason is the whole point: the pause menu is the one state you reach
when something looks wrong, and it is precisely the state in which you can no
longer read the dev readout, take a flight-recorder snapshot, or grab a
screenshot for a bug report. The diagnostic layer is disabled exactly when it is
needed. Same family as #1027's "silent wrongness" thesis, one step removed: the
instrument does not report anything false, it just silently stops existing.

## Options

**A. Elevate KeybindManager only (one line).**
`process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` in `keybind_manager.gd:_ready()`.
Hotkeys keep firing while paused. Cheapest. Incomplete: the overlays would
toggle visibility but their buttons stay unclickable, and it also un-pauses
screenshot/log-export/admin binds, which is probably desirable but is a wider
blast radius than "dev diagnostics".

**B. Elevate KeybindManager AND both overlays.** A plus
`PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` on `DevModeOverlay` (set in `dev_mode_overlay.gd:_ready()`
next to the existing `layer = OVERLAY_LAYER` at `:46`) and on the `DebugOverlay`
node. Delivers the actual ask -- diagnose *while* paused, buttons live. This is
my recommendation. Note the dev overlay's pokes mutate GameManager state while
the tree is paused; that is fine for a dev build (the pokes are already arbitrary
state edits) but should be a conscious call, not a side effect.

**C. Split the binds.** Give the DEBUG-category binds their own always-processing
dispatcher and leave gameplay binds pausable. Cleanest conceptually, most code,
and `keybind_manager.gd` already has a `Category.DEBUG` to key off. Overkill for
now; worth it if the always-on set later needs to differ from "all of them".

**D. Also make ESC yield when a dev surface is open.** Independent of A-C: have
`main_ui.gd:498-505` decline to open the pause menu if the dev overlay is
visible, so ESC closes the dev overlay first (standard LIFO). #1002 landed a
shared `ModalStack` chokepoint for exactly this kind of LIFO ordering -- the dev
overlay is currently outside it. Judgement call: if B lands, D matters much less,
because the overlay would remain usable under the pause menu anyway.

Not proposing a mandate. B+D is what I would pick; B alone gets 80% of the value
for one line each.

## Scope note

Dev-build-only surfaces (`BuildInfo.is_dev_build()` gates `dev_mode_overlay.gd:48`),
so nothing here changes the shipping player build. NOT league-blocking for Friday.
It does slow down every playtest bug report between now and then, which is the
real cost.

Related: #1002 (ModalStack LIFO chokepoint), #1011 (three docs disagree with
`keybind_manager.gd`), #1027.

issues.title: dev+ux: no way to replay the cold-open intro -- add a reset for last_seen_intro_version

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
Pip needs to replay the cold-open repeatedly while playtesting. Today there is no
in-game way to do that -- once seen, it is seen forever.

## Evidence (CONFIRMED)

- `godot/autoload/game_config.gd:110` -- `var last_seen_intro_version: String = ""`
  (`"" = never seen the cold-open`), persisted in the config `game` section.
- `godot/autoload/game_config.gd:151` -- `const INTRO_VERSION: String = "1"`,
  deliberately independent of `CURRENT_VERSION` so ordinary patches do not
  re-trigger the intro.
- `godot/autoload/game_config.gd:535-544` -- the whole gate:
  ```
  func should_show_intro() -> bool:
      if not play_intros:
          return false
      return last_seen_intro_version != INTRO_VERSION
  ```

So a reset is: set `last_seen_intro_version = ""` and `save_config()`. That is
the entire change. Nothing else reads the field. No migration, no versioning
concern, no ladder impact (this is presentation state, not run state).

Note the gate is already deliberately clean -- the comment at `:530-533` records
that it is gated PURELY on `last_seen_intro_version` and NOT on `games_played`,
specifically to be immune to the `increment_games_played()` ordering in
`config_confirmation.gd`. Whoever wrote #801 left this easy on purpose.

## Manual workaround for today (no code change)

Edit the persisted config and blank the value, then relaunch:

- Windows user config path is Godot's `user://` --
  `%APPDATA%/Godot/app_userdata/<project name>/` (the project name comes from
  `godot/project.godot`). Find the config file written by
  `GameConfig.save_config()`, locate the `game` section's
  `last_seen_intro_version`, set it to an empty string, save.

Setting it to any string other than `"1"` also works -- the gate is an
inequality, not an emptiness test. `play_intros` must also be true.

## Where should the control live? (options, not a mandate)

**A. Dev overlay button.** `godot/scripts/debug/dev_mode_overlay.gd` already
hosts a column of dev "pokes". A `Replay Intro` button there is the smallest,
lowest-risk change, ships in dev builds only, and directly serves the stated need
(Pip replaying it while playtesting). Downside: does nothing for players, and it
inherits the pause-interaction problem filed separately in the ESC/dev-overlay
issue.

**B. Settings menu entry.** `godot/scenes/settings_menu.tscn` +
`settings_menu.gd`, next to the existing `play_intros` toggle. Player-visible
("Replay intro"), which is a genuinely nice thing to have -- players who skipped
the cold-open on first run currently cannot ever see it. Downside: player-facing
UI change during a release freeze, needs a string and a layout slot.

**C. Both.** B for players, A for the tight playtest loop.

Recommendation: **A now** (dev-only, zero player-build risk, unblocks Pip's loop
this week), **B queued for after the Friday cut** as a small UX win. Do not do B
before the freeze lifts.

Either way, implement it as a single named function on GameConfig
(`reset_intro_seen()`) so both call sites share it and the field is not poked
from UI code.

## Size

Genuinely tiny -- one function on GameConfig plus one button. Filing it because
it is easy to lose, not because it is hard.

Related: #801 (the cold-open intro gate this reverses), #1028 (the pause/dev-overlay interaction referenced above).

issues.title: ui(bug): 'Game not started...' is the permanent first line of every player's feed; 'Turn 1' label is dead

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
Two concrete bugs found by the read-only scene audit in
`docs/UI_PLACEHOLDER_AUDIT_2026-07-30.md` (34 `.tscn` files, 224 `text =`
assignments classified). Filed together because they are the same defect class,
but only (a) reaches players.

## (a) PLAYER-FACING -- `Game not started...` is the permanent first line of every feed

CONFIRMED.

`godot/scenes/ui/watch_screen.tscn:25`:
```
[node name="MessageLog" type="RichTextLabel" parent="MessageScroll"]
text = "[color=gray]Game not started...[/color]"
```

The feed writer only ever appends:
- `godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:1359` -- `message_log.text += "\n" + line`

`grep -n 'message_log.text' godot --include=*.gd` returns exactly two writes:
that `+=`, and `main_ui.gd:1384` (`message_log.text = text`) inside
`_render_feed()`, which is a full rebuild but only runs on
`_on_feed_filter_changed` / `_on_rivals_filter_changed` -- i.e. only when the
player happens to toggle a feed filter.

Consequence: in a normal run the first line of the player's message log
permanently reads `Game not started...`, above every real event line. Harm is
modest (it scrolls out of view) but it is false state shipped to players, and it
is the same string that made the dead UI in #1023 look alive. It ships Friday
unless fixed.

It also explains its own survival: anyone who flipped a feed filter while testing
watched it silently disappear.

Fix: author the scene text empty, and add an unconditional clear on the boot path
in `main_ui.gd`. The unconditional `=` is the load-bearing half -- authoring it
empty alone would leave the same hole open for the next person.

## (b) DEV-VISIBLE ONLY -- `Turn 1` is never assigned; the node is hidden instead

CONFIRMED.

`godot/scenes/main.tscn:103`:
```
[node name="TurnCountLabel" type="Label" parent="TabManager/MainUI/TopBar"]
text = "Turn 1"
```

`godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:1060` does `turn_count_label.visible = false` (the
date badge at `TurnLabel` supersedes it; the merge is explained in the comment at
`main_ui.gd:1057`). The `.text` is written nowhere in the tree.

So: when the UI is alive the label is hidden; when boot fails the label is
visible reading `Turn 1`. No live-player impact -- but it is the worst-behaved
variant of the class, because the placeholder is displayed **only** in the
failure case. It contributed directly to #1023 reading as a gameplay bug rather
than a boot failure.

Fix: delete the `text` property (or the node -- it is dead UI). Not a sentinel
change; there is nothing to sentinel.

## The generalisable rule this exposes

**`+=` does not establish runtime ownership of a node's text.** Only an
unconditional `=` on a boot path does. Any node written exclusively via `+=` must
be authored empty in the scene and cleared explicitly at boot.

This rule matters beyond these two nodes: it is the one invariant that an
automated checker could use to distinguish "runtime owns this label" from
"runtime decorates this label", and it is why the audit's ownership-analysis
design (Design B) was the only proposed gate that would have flagged (a) at all.

## Priority

(a) is small but is live player-facing wrongness in the Friday build. (b) is
cosmetic-until-something-breaks and can ride any later cleanup.

Related: #1023 (the boot failure these dressed up), #1027 (silent wrongness as
the dominant failure mode), and #1031 (the remaining 30 DANGEROUS placeholders + the proposed sentinel convention).

issues.title: ui(tech-debt): 30 scene-authored placeholders read as real state -- sentinel convention, then a narrow gate

labels.name: technical-debt
labels.description: Technical debt that needs addressing

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
Follow-on from `docs/UI_PLACEHOLDER_AUDIT_2026-07-30.md`. **Read the doc** -- it
carries the per-line tables, the rejected alternatives, and the measured false
positive rates. This issue is the actionable summary.

The two LIVE bugs from the same audit are filed as #1030; this is everything else.

## What the audit found

34 `.tscn` files under `godot/` (excluding `addons/`), 20 with `text =`
properties, 224 assignments total.

| Category  | Count | Meaning |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| DANGEROUS |    32 | reads as real runtime state |
| AMBIGUOUS |     9 | judgement calls, argued individually in the doc |
| HARMLESS  |   183 | static chrome: captions, headings, legends, keybind hints |

Of the 32 DANGEROUS, 30 are overwritten by runtime code in normal operation --
so they are **debugging traps**, live only when boot fails, which is exactly what
happened in #1023. The other 2 are the live bugs in #1030.

Worst offenders in the 30, for flavour:
- `godot/scenes/main.tscn:240` -- `58.5%`. A specific, precision-carrying,
  plausibly-mid-game doom reading. Nothing about `58.5` says "not real".
- `godot/scenes/ui/staff_perks_panel.tscn:211,218` -- `DR. ELENA VANCE`,
  `Safety Researcher | Skill 7/10`. A fully realised fake employee.
- `godot/scenes/config_confirmation.tscn:97-165` -- the entire pre-launch review
  screen is convincing fakes of the exact values the screen promises to report,
  including `weekly-2025-w45`, a week from a year the game no longer starts in.
- `godot/scenes/ui/employee_screen.tscn:86` -- `[OK] No warnings`. A positive
  ASSERTION: a dead panel claims the team is fine.
- `godot/scenes/ui/whats_new_modal.tscn:85` -- `Version 0.11.0 - Travel &
  Conferences`, a stale wrong version number.

Aggravating detail from `main.tscn`: the placeholders do not even match the
runtime FORMAT (runtime money is `GameConfig.format_money(...)` with no
`Money: ` prefix; compute/research are bare `%.1f`). So a reader cannot
distinguish "dead UI" from "old build" either.

## Proposed convention

**A node whose text is owned by runtime code MUST be authored in the scene as one
of a closed set of ASCII sentinels, never as a specimen value.**

| Sentinel | Use |
|----------|-----|
| `""` (empty) | preferred where the empty node does not collapse layout |
| `--` | a value slot (numbers, money, percentages, dates, counts) |
| `[--]` | a bracketed-chrome value slot, matching `[M]` / `[OK]` / `[!]` |
| `???` | an unknown-identity slot (names, quirks, statuses) |
| `<Label>` | a named slot where sizing needs realistic width, e.g. `<doom>` |

This codifies an existing in-repo precedent rather than importing one: the tree
already ships `???`, `---`, `[---]`, `Researcher.HIDDEN_PLACEHOLDER` in
`staff_perks_panel`, and `Avg Score: --` at
`godot/scripts/ui/leaderboard_screen.gd:606-607`. Note that last one -- that
script's own empty state already writes `--` while its scene literals at
`leaderboard_screen.tscn:195-205` assert `0`. The scene disagrees with the
script's own house style.

Crucially it degrades LOUDLY: a boot-failed HUD reading `-- | -- | Phase: --`
cannot be mistaken for turn 1.

Rejected alternatives (reasoning in the doc): empty-by-default as the *sole*
rule (Godot layout genuinely needs non-empty text to size `HBoxContainer`
Labels); `PLACEHOLDER`/`TODO` words (too long, wrecks layout worse than a real
value); a node-naming convention (renaming breaks every `$Path/To/Node` and
`@onready` in the UI layer for zero runtime benefit, and fixes nothing for the
human staring at the screen).

## Recommended sequence -- ORDER IS THE POINT

1. Fix the two live bugs (#1030).
2. **Convert the 30 remaining DANGEROUS lines to sentinels.** This is the whole
   payoff and needs no tooling.
3. **THEN** add the gate as `tools/check_scene_placeholders.py`, pre-commit on
   changed `.tscn` plus a CI full-tree pass.
4. Do NOT build the ownership-cross-reference design (Design B in the doc):
   estimated 20-40% FP rate concentrated on the interesting multi-hop cases,
   days of effort, and it rots.

Step 3 must not precede step 2. A gate added first is red on arrival against 30
pre-existing lines, gets `--no-verify`-ed once, and is then ignored forever.
That is a worse outcome than no gate.

## Honest limitation of the proposed gate -- state this up front

The gate design that survives cost/benefit (Design A: flag `text = "..."` in
`.tscn` when the value contains a digit, restricted to `Label`/`RichTextLabel`,
after stripping colour hex and `[...]` bracket spans, skipping values over ~40
chars) measures at roughly **24 true positives / 1 false positive (~4%)** on the
current tree, versus 23/15 (39%) raw.

Its problem is recall, not precision. It structurally CANNOT catch the
non-numeric DANGEROUS values -- `DR. ELENA VANCE`, `AI Safety Lab`,
`Standard (Regulatory)`, `[SAFE]`, `Phase: Not Started`, `[OK] No warnings`,
and, most importantly, `Game not started...`.

**A digit gate would NOT have caught the incident that prompted this audit.**
Anyone selling it as the fix is overselling. The audit's own estimate: it
prevents maybe 60-70% of future instances of this class and roughly 0% of the
"plausible prose status line" variant that actually cost the debugging time.
Worth doing because it is cheap, not because it closes the hole.

## Implementation constraint for whoever builds the gate

The allowlist **cannot** be inline. Godot rewrites `.tscn` on save and drops
comments, so the `# scene-nav-allow` annotation trick used by
`tools/check_scene_nav.py` does not transfer. It must be an external checked-in
file (`tools/scene_placeholder_allowlist.txt`, entries like
`path/to/scene.tscn:NodePath`). That is extra friction, and it is the reason to
keep the gate narrow enough that the allowlist stays short.

One scene is correct by construction and should be allowlisted, not converted:
`godot/scenes/welcome.tscn:155` (`v0.13.1`) is overwritten at
`welcome_screen.gd:48` AND stamped by `tools/sync_version.py`, whose `--check`
gates pre-commit and CI.

## Priority

Not league-blocking. This is a debuggability investment, and its value is
entirely realised the next time something fails to boot during a release week.
Fits #1027's thesis directly: the existing guardrails are strong at preventing
bad code and weak at detecting wrong state.

Related: #1030 (the two live bugs from the same audit), #1023, #1026, #1027, #744 (the ASCII rule the sentinels respect), #1035 (the .tscn non-ASCII side finding, which shares the external-allowlist constraint).

issues.title: nomenclature: stale 'AP' vocabulary in player-facing text after the attention-economy migration (#996) -- scoped sweep + GLOSSARY.md is missing

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
Raised by Pip while playtesting 2026-07-30, verbatim:

> "still called AP in the dialogues in game, we should start sweeping for that, maybe as a wider nomenclature and player facing text drive?"

The AP (Action Points) pool was REMOVED on 2026-07-28 (#996) and replaced by
founder **Attention** plus typed founder hours (planning / operating). The code
migrated. The words did not.

This is not a find-and-replace ticket. `AP` -> `Attention` is wrong in several
places, because some of the surviving text describes a *mechanic* that no longer
exists, not just a *noun* that was renamed. And a third bucket must never be
touched at all.

## Bucket 1 -- PLAYER-FACING and WRONG (these are the ones that matter)

Text a player reads describing a mechanic that no longer exists. All verified as
NOT overwritten by runtime code unless noted.

### Event dialogue -- Pip's actual complaint

| Location | String | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `godot/scripts/ui/event_dialog.gd:78` | `parts.append("%d AP" % int(amount))` | The branch guard immediately above is `elif resource == "attention":`. The engine already speaks Attention; the label says AP. |
| `godot/scripts/ui/event_dialog.gd:257` | `missing_resources.append("AP (need %s, have %s available)" % [cost, available])` | Same -- inside `if resource == "attention":`. This is the "you cannot afford this" message. |

These two are literally "the code says attention, the player reads AP". Highest
confidence, most visible, cheapest fix.

### In-game help (teaches the wrong model outright)

| Location | String |
|---|---|
| `godot/scenes/player_guide.tscn:125` | `Actions cost Action Points (AP) and resources` |
| `godot/scenes/player_guide.tscn:184` | `6. [b]Action Points:[/b] Use all your AP each turn - wasted AP = wasted time` |

`:184` is worse than stale vocabulary -- it teaches a *strategy* ("use all your
AP each turn") for a resource that no longer exists, in a system where unspent
reserve evaporates at month end and the binding constraint is the planning /
operating hour split.

### Main screen chrome

| Location | String | Liveness |
|---|---|---|
| `godot/scenes/main.tscn:355` | `text = "Reserve AP"` (ReserveAPButton) | **LIVE.** `main_ui.gd:1175,1191` only touch `.disabled`; the text is never reassigned. |
| `godot/scenes/main.tscn:376` | `tooltip_text = "Execute queued actions and advance to next turn. Shows warning if you have unused AP."` | **LIVE.** `main_ui.gd:407` overwrites the button's `.text` to `COMMIT THE MONTH >` but never its `tooltip_text`. So the button says "commit the month" and its tooltip says "advance to next turn ... unused AP". |

### Feed / log lines the player reads

| `godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:868` | `log_message("[color=cyan]Reserving 1 AP for events...[/color]")` |

### Plan screen

The docstring three lines above (`:132`) already says "hold all Attention for
response windows". The surrounding prose migrated; the player-visible strings
did not.

### Travel / conference panel

| `godot/scripts/ui/travel_panel_controller.gd:519` | `submit_btn.text = "Submit Paper (1 AP)"` |
| `godot/scripts/ui/travel_panel_controller.gd:615` | `cost_label.text = "... \nTotal: %s + 2 AP"` |

### Content data

| Location | String |

| `godot/data/historical_timeline/2017.json:108` | `"text": "Organize safety reading group (costs 2 AP)"` |
| `godot/data/historical_timeline/2017.json:148` | `"text": "Integrate principles into lab policy (costs 2 AP, $10k)"` |

Loaded by `godot/scripts/data/timeline_loader.gd:14`
(`res://data/historical_timeline`). These are choice labels -- player-read, and

### Upgrade catalogue

| Location | String |

### Keybind UI

| Location | String |
|---|---|
| `godot/autoload/keybind_manager.gd:72` | `"commit_plan": {..., "description": "Commit Plan & Reserve AP"}` -- surfaced in the keybind/settings screen. See also #1011 (three docs already disagree with this file). |

**Bucket 1 total: 18 strings across 9 files.**

### Boot-failure-only, listed for completeness, NOT bucket 1

Two `main.tscn` lines say AP but are overwritten in normal play, so a player only
sees them if boot fails (i.e. #1023's failure mode):

- `godot/scenes/main.tscn:176` -- `text = "AP: 0"`, overwritten at
  `main_ui.gd:1112` with `Attention: %d (%d free, %d queued)`.
- `godot/scenes/main.tscn:177` -- `tooltip_text = "Action Points. Limits actions
  per turn. Base 3 + 0.5 per staff."`, overwritten at `main_ui.gd:1116` with the
  real Attention/hours tooltip.

Correcting a claim made when this was reported: `:177` is **not** live
player-facing text. It is still wrong and still describes removed mechanics
("Base 3 + 0.5 per staff" is exactly the dead pool formula), and it is on the
list -- it just belongs with the placeholder-sentinel work, not with the
player-facing sweep. Both lines are already in `docs/UI_PLACEHOLDER_AUDIT_2026-07-30.md`'s DANGEROUS table and are owned by #1031.

## Bucket 2 -- DEVELOPER-FACING (lower priority, still worth doing)

Dev overlays, debug strings, docstrings, identifiers. No player ever reads these;
they cost comprehension time for anyone (human or agent) reading the code.

| Location | Kind |
|---|---|
| `godot/scripts/debug/debug_overlay.gd:347` | `"Debug: Added 5 AP"` |
| `godot/scenes/debug_overlay.tscn:98` | `text = "Add 5 Action Points"` |
| `godot/scripts/debug/dev_mode_readout.gd:52` | `"AP: %d total \| %d avail \| %d committed \| %d reserved"` |
| `godot/scripts/game_manager.gd:322` | docstring `"""Purchase an upgrade - doesn't consume AP"""` |
| `godot/scripts/game_manager.gd:432` | docstring `"""Remove specific action from queue and refund its AP cost"""` |

Plus identifiers throughout: `ap_label`, `ap_cost`, `ap_text`, `ap_color_name`,
`reserve_ap()` (`game_manager.gd:385`), `_on_reserve_ap_button_pressed()`
(`main_ui.gd:866`), and the scene node names `APLabel`
(`godot/scenes/main.tscn:173`) and `ReserveAPButton`
(`godot/scenes/main.tscn:353`).

**Warning on the node names specifically:** renaming `APLabel` /
`ReserveAPButton` breaks `@onready var ap_label = $TopBar/APLabel`
(`main_ui.gd:13`), `$BottomBar/ControlButtons/ReserveAPButton`
(`main_ui.gd:39`), and the `[connection]` at `godot/scenes/main.tscn:418`. It
also requires editing `.tscn` files, which is off-limits during a freeze and is
pure churn. Recommend: rename identifiers and node names as a **separate,
post-league, single-purpose PR** or not at all. Do not bundle it with the
player-facing sweep -- mixing a risky rename into a text fix is how a cosmetic PR
becomes a regression.

`godot/tests/**` contributes a further 18 quoted-string AP hits. Same bucket,
lowest priority; they should follow whatever the identifiers do.

## Bucket 3 -- HISTORICAL and CORRECT: DO NOT SWEEP

**Changing any of these falsifies the record.** Anyone running a
search-and-replace must exclude them explicitly.

| Location | Why it must stay |
|---|---|
| `godot/data/patch_notes.json:26` | `"AP Double-Spend Bug - Actions no longer deduct AP twice"` -- describes what an old version did. |
| `godot/data/patch_notes.json:30` | `"Event Popup AP Display - Shows correct available AP"` |
| `godot/data/patch_notes.json:52` | `"Event AP Logic uses available AP correctly"` |
| `godot/data/patch_notes.json:56` | `"Turn Philosophy: 'Skip Turn' renamed to 'Commit Plan & Reserve AP'"` |
| `godot/data/balance/defaults.json:15` | `_description` states "as of T2 (2026-07-28) no legacy AP pool either: Attention is the ONLY founder currency". This is the correct, current, explanatory text -- it uses "AP" precisely to say the AP pool is gone. |
| `godot/scripts/core/actions.gd:552` | comment quoting the workshop ruling verbatim: `"staff never add founder AP"` |
| `godot/scripts/core/turn_manager.gd:87` | same quotation: `"the pool illusion dies; staff never add founder AP"` |
| `godot/scripts/core/office.gd:18` | quotes #791: `"predictable AP/cash sink"` |

The last three are **verbatim quotations of design rulings**. Editing the words
inside a quotation to match current vocabulary makes the citation false. If they
bother anyone, the correct treatment is to leave the quote intact and add a
bracketed gloss outside it, not to rewrite it.

## Bucket counts

| Bucket | Strings | Files |
|---|---|---|
| 1 -- player-facing and WRONG | 18 | 9 |
| 1b -- boot-failure-only (goes with the placeholder work) | 2 | 1 |
| 2 -- developer-facing strings | 5 | 3 (+ identifiers, + 18 test strings) |
| 3 -- historical, DO NOT TOUCH | 8 | 5 |

Raw totals for reference: `\bAP\b|Action Points?` matches 100 lines in
`godot/**/*.gd`, 7 in `godot/**/*.json`, 7 in `godot/**/*.tscn`. Most of the
`.gd` volume is identifiers and tests.

## Why this is a nomenclature drive, not a replace

Pip's instinct ("maybe as a wider nomenclature and player facing text drive?") is
the right frame, for a concrete reason visible in the table: several bucket-1
strings cannot be fixed by substituting a word.

- `player_guide.tscn:184` "Use all your AP each turn - wasted AP = wasted time"
  needs rewriting around the monthly grant, evaporating reserve, and the
  planning/operating split. There is no word that makes that sentence true.
- `main.tscn:376`'s tooltip says "advance to next turn" on a button labelled
  `COMMIT THE MONTH >`. The turn-vs-month vocabulary drifted separately from AP.
- `main.tscn:177` (boot-failure-only) states a formula, `Base 3 + 0.5 per staff`.
- "Reserve AP" as a *concept* still exists (holding Attention for response
  windows) but "reserve" may not be the right word for it any more -- that is a
  design call, not a text call.

So the sweep needs a decided vocabulary first, applied second. Which raises:

## Blocker: `docs/GLOSSARY.md` does not exist

CONFIRMED. `find . -iname "*glossary*"` over the repo returns nothing. Two
documents already reference it as though it does:

- `docs/art/ENDGAME_CONCEPT_REVIEW_2026-07-29.md:339` -- "Consider adding A9
  (poster art vs hero art) to `docs/GLOSSARY.md`"
- `docs/game-design/WS3_ENDGAME_RULINGS_2026-07-29.md:130` -- "Add the
  escalation-ladder vocabulary to `docs/GLOSSARY.md`; cross-index it"

This is #1027's pattern again, and #1018's: documents referring confidently to
things that are not there. The glossary needs to be created and to state
authoritatively what the current terms are -- Attention, planning hours,
operating hours, month vs turn vs day, reserve -- before a text sweep has
anything to sweep *toward*. That should probably be step 0 of this issue rather
than a separate ticket.

## Suggested sequence

1. Create `docs/GLOSSARY.md` with the current founder-economy vocabulary
   (Attention, planning/operating hours, monthly grant, reserve/evaporation) and
   the turn/month/day time model. Source of truth: `godot/data/balance/defaults.json:15`
   `_description`, ADR-0009/0011, and `main_ui.gd:1116`'s Attention tooltip,
   which is currently the single best plain-English statement of the mechanic in
   the repo.
2. Fix the two `event_dialog.gd` strings (`:78`, `:257`). Two lines, highest
   visibility, directly answers Pip's report.
3. Fix the remaining 16 bucket-1 strings, rewriting rather than substituting
   where the sentence describes dead mechanics.
4. Bucket 2 strings.
5. Identifiers and node names -- separate PR, post-league, or never.
6. Never touch bucket 3.

## League relevance

Steps 2 and 3 touch player-visible text in a build shipping Friday. They are
string-only changes with no logic or balance impact, so they are low-risk if
someone wants them in the cut -- but note that step 3 includes edits to
`godot/scenes/main.tscn` and `godot/scenes/player_guide.tscn`, which is scene
churn during a freeze. My read: **step 2 is worth taking (two `.gd` string
literals, near-zero risk, fixes the thing the tester actually noticed); steps 3+
should wait for the cut.** That is a call for Pip, not for me.

Related: #996 (the AP pool removal that stranded this vocabulary), #1011 (keybind
docs already disagree with `keybind_manager.gd`), #1018, #1027, and #1031 (owns `main.tscn:176-177`).

issues.title: playtest 2026-07-30 (v0.13.2 artifact): UI/UX findings from the Gate 4 run

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
Findings from Pip's recorded playtest of the **built 0.13.2 release artifact**, 2026-07-30 09:03, 9m06s. Transcript and frames in `art_generated/audiodump/` (gitignored).

The four league-critical ones were fixed same-day in PR #1039. **This issue holds the remainder** so they are scheduled rather than living in a recording nobody re-listens to -- the lesson of the pack-schema lane (#1018), which was never ticketed and therefore never happened.

Ordered by Pip's own emphasis, with timestamps so the audio can be checked.

## Nomenclature: "Turn" is counting days

**[1:44]** *"Stop having it fucking saying turn 21. It is either day 21 or the turn number is the number of like times we get into the planning mode."* And **[6:21]** *"Turn 133, that's wrong, I'm up to January 2018."*

The top-left counter increments per day, but is labelled Turn. Under the current model a turn is a planning cycle, not a day. This is a semantic fix with real surface area (the label, the tooltip, anything that reads it, and probably the leaderboard's "Turns" column, which per #1039 does correctly mean score). Wants a ruling on what a turn IS before any renaming. Related: #1037, and `docs/GLOSSARY.md` should carry the answer.

## Hiring and onboarding

- **[2:11]** The hiring pipeline screen needs to be roughly **double its size** -- "so we can see everything".
- **[2:21]** Hiring actions stack in the in-flight section but **do not create cards in the action queue**. Pip wants both, so priorities can be seen and rearranged.
- **[5:07]** The onboarding prompt fires only on the **offer -> accept** path. Other hiring routes complete with no prompt, and nothing directs the player to the onboarding section at all.
- **[5:37]** Make the hiring pipeline a more significant UI feature, easier to navigate in and out of. Same for the liability ledger.

## Screens that need more room

- **[6:51]** The global-leaderboard one-time-choice screen and the defeat screen should both be **about twice as big** -- information is being lost while dead space sits behind them.
- **[7:15]** Grey out the take-more-actions buttons until score submission is **confirmed**, not merely started.
- **[7:27]** The "press Enter for leaderboard" prompt is **below the fold** -- it needs scrolling to discover.

## Leaderboard presentation (beyond the #1039 column fix)

- **[7:36]** Default view is **local**; it should probably be **global**.
- **[7:54]** Player name and lab name display still need work.
- **[8:17]** **Highlight the viewer's own entry** with a horizontal band -- otherwise it is undifferentiated text.
- **[8:31]** Add **ABAB row striping** and **vertical grid lines**, applied through the colour schema so they stay consistent when the palette changes.

## Visual homes for two systems

**[5:47]** Both should stay greyed out in-game until they have a proper introduction -- a transition or scene, not a bare panel appearing:
- **Liability ledger** -- "a scribbled bit of paper... with an IOU at the top" as the basic version.
- **Onboarding pipeline** -- possibly a whiteboard. Background undecided.

The mobile phone already serves this role for the bank, so the pattern exists.

## Smaller

- **[0:13]** The What's New modal says **no patch notes available** for this version. First thing a player sees on a league build. `godot/data/patch_notes.json` has no 0.13.2 entry.
- **[0:19]** The dev-build badge (top right) is clipped; needs to move left to be readable.
- **[1:11]** A cat portrait renders as a magenta/black pattern at high doom. **Not** a missing texture -- verified the textures are in the `.pck` (`arwen` appears 8 times, 1004 `.ctex` entries). Likely a doom-level modulate. Pip: "not so much [a priority] but it's solveable".
- **[1:27]** The strategic-moves-unlocked popup needs a header, and is hardcoded to a fixed time.
- **[2:48]** Images spill over text in several panels.
- **[4:59]** Fundraising results resolve too fast -- wants them slowed.

## Already tracked elsewhere, listed so nobody re-files

Action queue overflow, leaderboard column off-by-one, the F8/N key, and the feed placeholder are all **fixed in #1039**. Placeholder convention is #1031; AP vocabulary is #1037; the intro replay Pip needs for repeat playtesting is #1029.

issues.title: Leaderboard: the Duration column is meaningless when the score is turns survived

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
From Pip's recorded playtest, 2026-07-31 **[4:49]**:

> *"Duration doesn't make sense, because these are all 6 and 13 seconds, so the duration column doesn't work."*

## The problem

The board shows real elapsed wall-clock time. The score is **turns survived** (ADR-0002). A column reading "6s" / "13s" next to a turns-survived ranking invites the reader to compare two runs on a number that means nothing about how well either was played -- and a fast clicker looks better than a careful one.

Worse on a league board where the whole point is comparability.

## Options

1. **Drop the column.** Smallest, honest.
2. **Replace with something that ranks**: doom integral (already the ADR-0002 tiebreak and already submitted), or turns.
3. **Keep it but label it as trivia**, visually demoted so nobody reads it as a ranking signal.

Recommend 1 or 2 -- an unremovable number on a leaderboard is read as a score whatever the header says.

## Note

`duration` is computed and submitted in `game_over_screen._persist_and_submit_score`. Removing the **column** is a display change; removing the **field** touches the submission contract, which is frozen per website #191. Do the display half only until the freeze lifts.

Source: `art_generated/audiodump/2026-07-31_10-24-00.transcript.md`

issues.title: Let the player set player name + lab name on the FIRST screen (not only in setup)

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
From Pip's recorded playtest, 2026-07-31 **[13:40]**:

> *"it's critical that we put the player name and lab name in there, it's critical that we let people update that on the first screen."*

And **[6:28]**: cannot click a name field to change it.

## Two halves, and only one is already tracked

- **Display** the name + lab on the board -- covered by #812 and #957.
- **Update them on the first screen** -- this issue. Not obviously covered anywhere.

## Why it matters tonight and after

Identity is what makes a leaderboard entry mean anything to the person who earned it. A player who reaches the board under a stale or default name has no reason to care about the board. The remote submission is gated on a non-empty player + lab name (`_has_submittable_identity`), so a player who never finds where to set them is a player whose score **silently does not upload**.

That is the failure family from #1027: nothing errors, the run just never appears.

## Ask

An editable name + lab field on the first screen the player sees, not only behind pre-game setup. Plus: check the [6:28] report that a name field is unclickable -- if a field is present but dead, that is a separate bug and the more urgent half.

Source: `art_generated/audiodump/2026-07-31_10-24-00.transcript.md`

issues.title: bug(window): minimising v0.13.2 does not minimise -- window left in a wrong state until re-maximised (first run after #1079)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
From the recorded playtest of the freshly built v0.13.2, 2026-08-01 09:52 (`art_generated/audiodump/2026-08-01_09-52-08.transcript.md`, local-only/gitignored; frames in `frames_2026-08-01_09-52-08/`).

## Observation

**[1:02]** "I'm going to minimise the screen, and then, that's interesting, well, I mean, that's probably not expected behaviour"
**[1:16]** "Okay, now I'm going to maximise it, so, that one was a bit of an interesting fix"

Frame `f005_64s.jpg` (~2s after the minimise attempt) shows the game still occupying the full screen -- the main menu fully rendered, cursor parked at the top-right where the window buttons live. Whatever "minimise" did, the window did not go to the taskbar; Pip had to re-maximise to get back to a good state (`f006_78s.jpg` looks normal again). Between f004 (before) and f005 (during), the menu renders at a visibly different scale, consistent with the window having restored to a different size/mode rather than minimising.

## Why this is flagged as a possible #1079 interaction

This is the FIRST run of a build containing PR #1079, which rewrote the corner build badge (`godot/scripts/ui/dev_build_badge.gd`) and newly connects `get_viewport().size_changed` to a refit callback that runs on every window resize -- minimise included. Reading the diff: the callback only recomputes the badge panel's own offsets, so a mechanism where it blocks or reverses a window minimise is not apparent. The badge itself renders correctly in every frame.

**Not diagnosed.** The recording shows the symptom but not the cause. Alternative candidate: engine/window-mode behaviour -- the game has no window mode options at all (#820), and how the project handles minimise/restore under whatever mode the release build launches in has never been specified.

Secondary observation from the same frames: the version label appears TWICE on the main menu -- the #1079 quiet corner badge top-right AND a second `v0.13.2` bottom-right (the welcome screen's own stamped label). One of them is redundant now.

## Ask

1. 30-second repro on the v0.13.2 release artifact: maximise, minimise, watch what happens. If it reproduces, capture window mode + what state the window lands in.
2. If it is the badge's `size_changed` handling, fix there; if it is window-mode handling, fold into #820's scope.
3. Decide which of the two version labels survives.

## Not claimed

- Not claiming #1079 caused it -- the diff gives no mechanism for it. Flagged because it is the only window-adjacent change in this build.
- Not claiming the game was unusable -- re-maximising recovered it immediately.

Related: #1079 (badge rewrite), #820 (window mode options), #1041 (previous playtest's findings).

issues.title: ux(hiring): onboard-now window -- tooltip omits the Attention cost (costs dict has money only), prints raw 'money: 3000.0', and Q/W read as the same option

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
From the recorded playtest of v0.13.2, 2026-08-01 09:52 (`art_generated/audiodump/2026-08-01_09-52-08.transcript.md`, local-only; frames in `frames_2026-08-01_09-52-08/`, see `f014_133s.jpg`, `f015_142s.jpg`, `f018_168s.jpg`).

The "Owen Rodriguez said yes" onboarding window (the new hiring-stitch accept prompt) works as a mechanic -- but four presentation defects landed together in one 35-second stretch:

## 1. The tooltip omits the Attention cost and prints a raw float

**[2:11]** "first bug ... this says 3 attention reserved and says it costs 3 money, this is not a really good layout"

Frame `f015_142s.jpg`: hovering `[Q] Set them up now (3 Att from reserve) ($3,000)` shows a tooltip reading `Costs: money: 3000.0`. Mechanism, verified in code: `godot/scripts/core/hiring_pipeline.gd:597` builds the option as `"costs": {"money": money}` -- the Attention cost lives only in the label TEXT, not in the structured costs dict, so whatever renders the costs tooltip can only ever show money. The tooltip also renders the internal key and float verbatim (`money: 3000.0`) instead of `$3,000`.

The tooltip additionally OCCLUDES the [W] option's label while hovering [Q] (visible in the frame), hiding exactly the text that distinguishes the two options.

## 2. Q and W read as the same option

**[2:20]** "the Q option is not a good layout, the W option is not a good layout"

The two labels are `[Q] Set them up now (3 Att from reserve) ($3,000)` and `[W] Set them up now (3 Att, pull from planned work) ($3,000)` -- identical first four words, identical price, the load-bearing difference buried mid-parenthesis. The reserve-vs-cannibalize choice is the crisp teaching moment of the window system (per `hiring_pipeline.gd:550` comment) and the layout hides it.

## 3. An unpayable option is offered, then errors after the click

**[2:34]** "Can I pull from planned work ... I can't pull from planned work, whatever"

Frame `f018_168s.jpg`: after choosing [W], an error line appears under the options: `[!] Insufficient capacity to handle by cannibalizing -- pick another option.` The message source is `godot/scripts/core/window_resolver.gd:91`; the option existed but could not be paid (`month_controller.gd:298` documents exactly this state). The window should know at render time that cannibalize cannot be paid (no free capacity, no WIP at turn 3) and show the option disabled with the reason, instead of letting the player pick it and bounce.

## 4. "Cannibalizing" is internal vocabulary leaking to the player

**[2:46]** "Insufficient capacity to handle by cannibalizing, okay"

`handle_reserve` / `handle_cannibalize` are the ENGINE's verb names (`window_resolver.gd:6`). "Cannibalizing" in a player-facing error, with no prior introduction of the term, reads as jargon. The player-facing copy should say what it means: "not enough unplanned capacity -- you would have to cancel planned work, and there is none to cancel".

## Ask

- Put the Attention cost into the costs dict (or teach the tooltip renderer to read both), and format money as money.
- Restructure the two set-up-now options so the SOURCE is the visible difference (e.g. one action, source picker).
- Disable-with-reason unpayable options at render time.
- Copy pass on the cannibalize failure text.

## Not claimed

- Not claiming the mechanic is wrong -- reserve-vs-cannibalize as an explicit choice is working as designed and Pip used it. This is presentation.

Related: #789 (the hiring stitch that built this window), #1041 (previous playtest hiring findings), #830 (hiring statefulness), #855 (Attention readout in event-dialog corner).

```
  StealthAI (rumored) (balanced) -- capabilities flat
```

**[3:58]** "Now, I've never seen these rivals before, this is the first time this information has appeared in the game"
**[4:02]** "So, we need to think something along the lines of, from a player experience, how do I know that I have rivals? And how has the game told me this? How has the game introduced this concept to me? How do I know what they're doing?"
**[4:18]** "This summary was probably done pre-W3, and so this needs a rework"

Three named organisations, with focus tags and a capability-drift read, appear for the first time in a recap popup -- as if the player already knew who they were. There was no introduction event, no feed beat announcing their existence, no screen where rivals live. (The feed HAS a "Hide rival intel" toggle, visible in `f014_133s.jpg`, so rival intel lines exist as a channel -- but a filter toggle is not an introduction either.)

## Mechanism

`godot/scripts/game_manager.gd:784` `_build_rivals_review_section()` builds the block from "each VISIBLE rival" -- so a visibility model already exists in the data. What does not exist is any moment that takes a rival from invisible to visible IN THE FICTION. Visibility flips somewhere in state; the player experiences it as the summary suddenly assuming context.

## Ask (design, then content)

1. An introduction beat per rival: the first time a rival becomes visible, that is an EVENT -- a feed story or window ("A lab in [city] published a capabilities result...", intel purchase, journalist call), not a bullet in a recap. Pip: "this is like a UI interaction storyline thing, so I think we can crack that out pretty quickly" [4:27].
2. The month-review rivals block should only ever RESTATE rivals the player has met, and say what changed since last month ("capabilities flat" three times at first appearance carries no information).
3. A place rivals live between summaries -- even one line each somewhere inspectable -- so "how do I know what they're doing?" has an answer.

## Not claimed

- Not claiming the rivals sim is wrong -- only its narrative surfacing. The summary text itself Pip liked as a format ("Staff 1, okay, that's cool, rivals this month" [3:55]).
- Not claiming where the intro should fire from -- that is a W3-flavoured design call (event tiers per ADR-0012 look like the natural home).

Related: the rivals-surfacing work from the success-premortem workstream (PRs #725/#726 territory), #825 (event OUTS sweep), #1016 (provenance real infrastructure failures as flavour), #956 (mysterious-stranger delivery pattern -- an existing example of introducing a channel in-fiction).

issues.body:
From the recorded playtest of v0.13.2, 2026-08-01 09:52 (`art_generated/audiodump/2026-08-01_09-52-08.transcript.md`, local-only; frame `f046_307s.jpg`).

## Observation

**[5:05]** "I want a visual, like a poster or a pop-up on the strategic moves unlocked ... This is a cool pop-up thing, but it's also like, well cool, it's just a black little screen, let's make that visually more interesting"

Frame `f046_307s.jpg`: the STRATEGIC MOVES UNLOCKED moment -- "The council of elders has deemed your standing sufficient. High-stakes plays now open to you..." -- renders as centered white text on a dimmed black overlay with a plain Continue button. The copy is doing milestone work; the visuals are doing nothing. This is (with the cold open) the game's biggest single fanfare beat, roughly a year into a run.

Code: `godot/scripts/ui/fanfare_popup.gd` (invoked from `main_ui.gd:1847` with the "STRATEGIC MOVES UNLOCKED" strings). The popup component is generic; it has no art slot.

## Ask

1. Give `fanfare_popup.gd` an optional hero/poster image slot.
2. Commission or promote a poster-style asset for the strategic-moves beat (the endgame poster batch pipeline in #1024 and the gpt-image-1 pipeline are the obvious generators; the in-repo art review flow decides the winner).
3. While in there: the same popup pattern presumably serves other milestone beats -- audit which fanfares exist and which deserve art, so this is one pattern fix, not one screen fix.

## Not claimed

- Not claiming the unlock TIMING or nomenclature is right -- that is #763's scope (month-grain pacing + "align fanfare hero"). This issue is purely the visual treatment of the popup surface. If #763's audit lands first, do the art second; they do not block each other.

Related: #763 (pacing/nomenclature for the same beat), #1024 (poster batch under provisional art rules), #817 (cold-open hero backgrounds -- sibling fanfare surface).
